text: Priya was late for the train and the platform was loud. She held up her phone and said, 'Could you please pick up my cooking podcast where I stopped yesterday, and play it a little faster, because I only have twelve minutes before my stop and I really want to hear the end?' The phone found the episode she had left halfway through. It said, 'I found Kitchen Talk, episode forty. You stopped at twenty-one minutes. I will start there and make the speed one and a half times faster.' Priya smiled as a smooth voice began to talk about how soda is made. She stepped onto the train, found a seat, and listened until her stop.

Someone wants to know how long the drive home will take.
Drive time?
How long till I'm home?
What does the traffic look like on the way back?
I have to sweep the bathroom before guests come, so when will I get home if I leave now?
Tell me the trip time to my house, please.
Is the road home busy right now?
How many minutes is it to my place?
Check the digital map and tell me how long I'll be on the road.
Would you mind telling me how long it will take to drive home with today's traffic?

Rosa got home from the hospital at eight in the morning, tired and hungry. She sat on the couch and said, 'Hey, where is my box of vegetables? I want it before this evening, because I have to chop a lot for soup.' The assistant checked her orders. It said, 'Your vegetable box is out for delivery. It should arrive between two and four this afternoon.' Rosa said, 'Can it come sooner? Half a day is too long to wait. And tell them to leave it at the front door.' The assistant said it could not make the truck go faster, but it added a note to leave the box at the front door. It promised to send a message when the driver was close. Rosa smiled, closed her eyes, and slept.

name: trim_video_clip
does: Cuts a short piece out of a longer video so it can be saved or shared.
inputs: the video, the time where the piece starts, and the time where it ends
people say:
- Cut out the part where the butterfly lands
- Make this video shorter, I only want the last minute
- Keep just the sharp part from ten seconds in to thirty
- I paid for this film, but I only want the first scene
- Trim it so it's easy to send to Mum

Someone wants the pool water to be warmer.
Warm the pool up.
Heat the water to twenty-eight degrees.
It snowed last night and the water feels icy, can you fix that?
I have a booking for a pool party at noon, so please get the water ready.
Turn on the heater.
I'd be lucky to find the water above twenty, so make it nicer to swim in.
It's too cold to get in, do something about it.
Could you please raise the pool temperature a few degrees before the kids come?

A text message is a short note you send from your phone to another person. People use texts when a call feels like too much, or when the other person may be asleep. A smart phone can read a new text out loud and write one when you speak. People change small things about it: who gets the message, when it is sent, and how loud the sound is. To change them they say things like, 'Text Dan that I'm ten minutes late,' 'Read my last message,' or 'Send it tomorrow morning, so it won't wake him.' Some say, 'Tell her I'm a mile away.' Group chats work the same way, but many people get the note. To quiet a noisy group, people say, 'Be quiet about this chat.'

name: warm_up_car
does: Starts the engine and heats the inside of the car before a trip.
inputs: which car, and what time you plan to leave
people say:
- I'm leaving soon, get the car ready
- It's freezing out, make the car cosy for the morning
- Start the engine at seven so I'm not cold
- I need to zoom to the vet with the puppy, heat up the car
- I'm tired of scraping ice, get the windows clear

Someone wants the news on the radio.
Put the news on.
I want to hear what's happening today.
Anything new in the world?
I haven't heard the headlines yet.
Tune to the news station, please.
While I stir this spicy soup, could you find the news?
I'm going fishing in an hour and feel out of touch with everything.
What's going on out there?
It's very quiet in here and I'd like to know what the world is up to.

name: lock_door
does: Locks a door of the house and says when it is done.
inputs: which door, and when to lock it
people say:
- Please lock the red door at the side of the house
- Lock up for the night
- Make sure nobody can get in tonight
- I forgot to lock up, can you do it for me?
- Grandpa is out in the yard to plant flowers, keep the front door shut till he's back

Marco was at the stove with flour on his hands when he looked at his list. 'My list is a mess,' he said to the kitchen speaker. 'The things I already did are still sitting at the front, and I can't see what is left.' The speaker understood that he wanted the finished tasks cleared out of the way. It said, 'I will check off the done items and move them to the bottom. Three tasks are left.' It read them out: buy flour, call Dad, and load the dishwasher. A little signal chimed when it was done. Marco nodded and kept stirring, glad that the list was short again.

Someone wants the computer to restart later.
Restart it.
Reboot the laptop tomorrow at seven.
Turn the computer off and on again at noon.
Please restart the downstairs computer after the update is installed tonight.
Can you restart this machine in an hour?
I'm going to bed, so start it fresh at six in the morning.
My gram uses the old computer downstairs, so make it fresh by eight tomorrow.
It's slow, so reboot it on Friday at nine.

A computer's battery keeps it running when it is not plugged in. When the charge gets low, the screen goes dim and a warning shows. People change a few things to make the battery last longer. They make the screen less bright, close programs they do not use, or turn on a saver mode. Some people set it by hand with a manual switch, while others let the computer decide. They say, 'Dim the screen,' 'Save my battery,' or 'How much charge is left?' Someone eating oatmeal at the breakfast table might say, 'Turn on battery saver, I want to visit my sister and I'll be on the train all day.'

name: guest_list
does: Keeps the list of people coming to a party and tells you how many have said yes.
inputs: the name of the party, and the name of the guest
people say:
- Who's coming on Saturday?
- Put Nina down as a yes
- How many people have said they'll come?
- Take Joe off, he can't make it
- Mia will bring a lamp for the garden, write that next to her name
- Tidy up the list, there are two Sams

name: boil_water
does: Heats the kettle and tells you when the water is hot.
inputs: how hot the water should be, and when to start
people say:
- I need hot water
- Get the kettle going
- Have it ready in five minutes for tea
- Is the water done yet?
- I'm walking a kilometer to the shop, so have the kettle hot when I get back
- Set it to eighty degrees, green tea is fine that way

Dana was eating lunch at her desk when she remembered the eggs at home. She typed to her phone in a hurry: 'how long do i boil eggs so thye are hard'. The assistant understood she wanted a cooking time for hard eggs. It answered, 'Put them in boiling water for ten minutes, then move them to cold water.' Dana typed again: 'text kim to turn on the vent and start the pot, the kitchen air is stale'. The assistant sent a text to Kim that said, 'Please turn on the vent and start the pot. The kitchen air is stale.' It also set a ten minute timer for Dana. She went back to her salad and felt relieved.

A radio picks up voices and music from the air. Each station has a number, and people turn a knob or press a button to find the one they like. They change the station, the volume, and sometimes save favorites so the radio can store them. When the sound is not clean and there is a hiss, people move the dial slowly until the voices come through. A slow, careful turn works best. People ask for changes in many ways. They say, 'Put on something calm,' 'Louder, please,' 'Go back to the last station,' or 'Keep this one.' In a car, someone may even say, 'I can't hear the talking,' and mean the same thing.

Someone wants to call their mother.
Call Mom.
Ring Mom.
Get my mother on the phone.
Dial Mum, please.
I want to talk to my mother.
I've shut the shop for the day, so please call my mum now.
The weather is mild and I'm on the porch, so I'd like to speak with my mother.
Could you please phone my mum and put her on speaker?

Person: Could you please put some thick bacon on my shopping list, because I'm cooking breakfast for the whole family on Sunday and we always run out?
Assistant: Of course. How many packs should I write down?
Person: Two packs. And a leg of lamb for the weekend too.
Assistant: Done. Which day will you cook the lamb?
Person: Saturday. Can you shuffle the list so the meat is at the top?
Assistant: Yes, the bacon and the lamb are now first.

Mr. Okafor, a retired teacher, stood at the window looking at his garden. 'The soil looks like a desert and the tomatoes are drooping,' he said to the speaker. A package of new seeds had come that morning, and he wanted the flat beds wet before he planted them. The assistant understood that he wanted water for the garden. It said, 'I will turn on the sprinkler for ten minutes.' Then it asked, 'Would you like me to change the schedule so it waters at six every morning?' Mr. Okafor said yes. The sprinkler began to hiss, and he went to get his gloves.

Lily, who was eight, sat on the sofa with a sad face. 'It's so quiet and boring,' she told the tablet. 'I finished my last book and the library is shut today.' The tablet understood that she wanted something to read. It said, 'I can read you a story. Do you want one about a dragon or one about a fox?' Lily said, 'The dragon, please.' The tablet began to read in a soft voice about a small dragon who was afraid of fire. Lily lay back on the cushions and listened until the story was finished. Then she asked for another.

A focus timer helps people work without stopping too often. You pick a short block of time, like twenty-five minutes, and work until it rings. Then you take a short break. People change the length of the block, the length of the break, and how many rounds to do. They also use it for small jobs at home. If bread is in the oven, a timer tells you when it is ready. When you are not sure how long a job will take, you can estimate and then change the time later. People say, 'Start a thirty minute timer,' 'Make my breaks five minutes,' or 'Give me ten more minutes.'

Someone wants ideas for decorating the house for the winter holidays.
Decoration ideas?
How should I decorate this winter?
Give me something to hang on the door.
Explain a simple way to make the house look festive.
Help me decorate.
Any weird but fun ideas for the tree?
Could you suggest a few ideas for the living room, nothing too expensive?
Tell me what I can put in the window.
The house looks so plain right now.

A medicine reminder is a gentle alert that tells an older person when to take a pill. It is for people who forget, or who take many different pills in a day. The alert can be a sound, a voice, or a message to a family member. People change the time, the name of the pill, and who gets told. They say things like, 'Remind Grandma at eight each morning,' 'Let me know when she has taken it,' or 'Call me if she doesn't answer.' In August, when families travel, someone far away may ask for a special check each evening, so they know everything is fine at home.

Jonah was lying in bed with his phone, typing fast. 'cancel my alarm for tomorrow,' he wrote. 'the roads are icy so school starts late, and my uncle's wife is driving me at ten.' The assistant understood that he wanted his morning alarm turned off. It answered, 'I cancelled your seven o'clock alarm. Do you want a new one?' Jonah typed, 'yeah wake me at nine, twenty-five min before we leave.' The assistant set the alarm for nine, and said it would sound softly and get louder. Jonah put the phone down, pulled up his blanket, and fell asleep.

Nadia, who cooked at a small cafe, sat at the kitchen table with a scarf she was knitting for her uncle. She had spilled tea near her bag, and the scarf was only half finished. 'I can't remember what comes after the third row,' she said to the speaker. 'I'm completely stuck.' The assistant understood that she wanted help with the next step of her pattern. It said, 'Your pattern says to knit two rows, then purl one. Do you want me to read the steps one at a time?' Nadia said yes, wiped the table, and picked up her needles.

Tom was a busy dad with two hungry kids and a thin wallet. At the grocery door, he told his phone, 'I hate fish, and the kids won't eat anything spicy, so no fish and no spice this week. Plan five dinners for me.' The assistant understood that he wanted a week of simple, cheap meals without those two things. It said, 'Here is a plan: pasta with tomato sauce, chicken and rice, bean tacos, vegetable soup, and baked potatoes. I left out fish and spice.' Tom said, 'Be patient with me, I may change the soup.' The assistant was patient, and said it could swap any dinner he liked.

Person: I want to send a text to my daughter, but I don't want a long one.
Assistant: Of course. What would you like it to say?
Person: Begin with hello and tell her I'm coming this winter.
Assistant: Which day should I say you are coming?
Person: Not a day yet. Just the season. My glasses are loose and I can't see the screen well, so please read it back.
Assistant: Here it is: Hello, I am coming to see you this winter. Should I send it?
Person: Yes, please send it.
Assistant: Sent to your daughter.

Kai had been playing games for hours when his stomach made a loud noise. 'There's nothing in the oven and nothing in the fridge,' he typed to his phone. 'Mom taught me never to eat chips for dinner.' The assistant understood that he wanted food brought to the house. It said, 'Do you want your regular order from Tony's Pizza, a large with cheese?' Kai typed, 'yes pls.' The assistant placed the order and said, 'It will arrive in about thirty minutes. I added a tip, as you usually do.' Kai put the phone down and went to set the table.

Carl, a driver, parked his truck and looked at his phone. 'I have more jobs than time today,' he said. The assistant checked his to-do list and found six tasks. It read them: go to the bank, fold the laundry upstairs, fix the mirror, call the garage, pick up bread, and wash the truck. Carl said, 'Do the shortest ones first, and move the laundry to tomorrow.' The assistant sorted the list so the quick jobs came first, and moved the laundry to the next day. Now only five tasks were left for today, and Carl started with the bank.

Someone wants the heating turned up and a message when the room is warm.
Warm it up.
Turn up the heat and send me a note when the room is toasty.
It's cold in here.
Raise the speed of the fan heater and shut the vent, please.
The air is so dry and chilly, please make the living room warmer.
Could you heat the bedroom and the hall, please?
I'm coming home soon, get the house cosy.
Push the thermostat up a few degrees, if you don't mind.

A robot mower cuts the grass by itself while the family does other things. It drives over the lawn in lines, turns at the edges, and goes back to its station when it needs to charge. People change how often it works, how short the grass should be, and when it should stay in. They say things like, 'Mow the lawn on Saturday,' 'Cut it a little shorter,' or 'Do not go out if it rains.' If the grass grows fast, they may say, 'Double the mowing this week.' A light rain is fine for most mowers, but a heavy storm means it should stay home.

Sam, a driver, was on his break in the freezing cold, with a hot drink in his hands. 'Tell me when my parcel comes,' he said to his phone. Then he stopped. 'Wait, not mine. It's my sister's parcel, the one with the blue scarf.' The assistant understood that he wanted a warning about his sister's delivery. It said, 'I will warn you when your sister's parcel is delivered. The price on the label is twenty dollars, and it needs a signature.' Sam said, 'Perfect, I'll be home by five.' The assistant said it would send a message at five if the parcel had not come.

Jess was late for work, with her bag half open and her keys in her hand. 'Lock the front door and the back door, and check the garage too,' she said. The assistant checked all three. It said, 'The front door and back door are now locked. The garage is open.' Jess said, 'Close it, and leave the hall light on for an hour more, because I need to pay the man who fixes the curtain rail.' The assistant closed the garage and kept the light on. Jess ran down the steps and got into her car, knowing the house was safe.

Someone wants eggs on the shopping list.
Put eggs on the list.
Twelve eggs, please.
We're out of eggs.
Write down two dozen cheap eggs, a flood of guests is coming on Sunday.
I have a ticket for the egg sale at the market, so write eggs on my list.
Don't let me forget eggs.
The fridge has no eggs left.
Could you please note that I need eggs for breakfast?

Ben was at his desk, sipping a creamy latte, when his phone buzzed again. 'This camera keeps pinging me every time a leaf moves,' he said to the assistant. 'I can't get anything done.' The assistant understood that he wanted the alerts to stop for a while. It said, 'I will mute the garden camera for one hour.' Then it asked, 'Do you want a link to the live view, in case you want to look?' Ben said yes. The assistant sent the link to his phone, and the buzzing stopped. Ben went back to his work, and the phone stayed quiet until lunch.

name: party_budget
does: Keeps a list of what you have spent on a party and shows the total so far.
inputs: what you bought, and how much it cost
people say:
- I swiped my card for the cake, put down forty dollars
- What's the total so far?
- How much have we used?
- The music was free, so take that sum off
- Write down balloons, twelve dollars
- Tell me when we pass two hundred

Eva woke up with a groan, before her alarm was even finished. 'When is the electric bill due?' she asked the speaker. 'No wait, the water bill.' The assistant understood that she wanted the water bill, not the electric one. It said, 'Your water bill is due on the twelfth. That is close, only three days from now. It is forty-six dollars.' Eva said, 'Pay it today.' Downstairs a neighbor started to shout at a dog, and she almost missed the answer. The assistant said, 'I will pay it this afternoon and send you a note.' Eva fell back onto her pillow.

Person: Could you please change the weight on my recipe, because I am going to jog home and shop on the way, and I need to know how much to buy?
Assistant: Sure. What does the recipe say, and what do you want it in?
Person: It says five pounds of potatoes. I want kilos.
Assistant: Five pounds is about two and a quarter kilos.
Person: Thank you. So a whole bag of two and a half kilos is enough?
Assistant: Yes, a bag of two and a half kilos will cover it.

Hana sat at her office desk, looking at the clock. 'Could you please book me a ride to the train station for six tonight?' she asked her phone. 'And I would like the car to pick me up one block away at the corner, because the front street is closed for roadwork and it is not easy for cars to get in.' The assistant understood that she needed a ride at six, with a pickup at the corner. It said, 'I booked a car for six o'clock at the corner of Pine Street. The driver is named Luis, and he will arrive in about four minutes before.' Hana smiled and kept working, sure she would catch her train.

Leo was bored of painting the kitchen when he heard a hiss. He turned and saw water begin to pour from a pipe under the sink. 'Call the plumber, quick!' he shouted at his phone. 'The pipe is leaking, I need someone in twenty minutes!' The assistant understood that this was an emergency. It said, 'I am calling Fast Fix Plumbing now. Turn off the water at the main valve, near the front door.' The plumber answered, and the assistant told him the address. He said he could come in twenty-five minutes. Leo ran to the valve and turned it, and the water slowed down to a drip.

The clock on the wall at the foot of the stairs shows the time where you live. The sun does not rise at the same moment everywhere, so a clock in another city shows a different time. People call these areas time zones. When someone travels, they adjust their watch to match the new place. Time itself keeps moving at a constant pace, but the number on the clock changes. People ask, 'What time is it in Tokyo?', 'Is it morning in London?', or 'Set my clock to local time.' It helps them call friends far away without waking them up.

Someone wants a recipe made twice as big.
Double the recipe.
Make this serve twice as many.
I have too many guests, I can't breathe, make the recipe bigger.
Two times the amounts, please.
My knee hurts and I'd rather not work it out the manual way, so change all the numbers for eight people.
How much flour do I need if I make double?
Rewrite it for twice the servings, if you don't mind.
I need more of everything, there are ten of us tonight.

name: parking_time_left
does: Tells you how long until your parking runs out and reminds you before it does.
inputs: where you parked, and the time your parking ends
people say:
- How long do I have left on the meter?
- Remind me before my parking runs out
- Do I owe more money for this space?
- Warn me ten minutes before I have to move the car
- I left my backpack in the car, how long until I must go back?
- Most places let you stay two hours, what about here?

Maria's kids sat on the loose cushions of the sofa, waiting. 'Find a movie for the kids, something with a kitten,' she said to the tv. 'No, wait, a puppy. They like puppies more.' The assistant understood the correction. It said, 'I found a film called Little Paws, about a puppy. It is ninety minutes long and good for all ages.' Maria asked, 'Is it a happy one? They grow bored fast with sad movies.' The assistant said it was funny and warm. Maria told it to start the movie. The kids cheered, and she went to make popcorn.

Lena was folding laundry when her young son ran in. 'How do you say jump and dance in Spanish?' he asked the speaker. The assistant understood that he wanted two Spanish words. It said, 'Jump is saltar. Dance is bailar.' The boy repeated them and began to jump and spin around the room. Lena laughed and said, 'Remind us tomorrow at seven to practice these words again.' The assistant set a reminder for tomorrow at seven, and said it would ask the boy to say each word out loud. Lena kept folding, and her son kept dancing.

Mrs. Hale, a retired teacher, sat on her porch with a hammer next to her. 'Remind me to feed Rex at five,' she said to her phone. 'And fill his huge water bowl, because I will mow the lawn first.' The assistant understood that she wanted two reminders for the dog. It said, 'I set a reminder at five for dinner and a bowl refill. Rex also needs his walk. Do you want a reminder for that?' Mrs. Hale said, 'Yes, twenty minutes after dinner.' The assistant added it. She picked up her hammer to fix the pet door, and then went to start the mower.

name: book_haircut
does: Finds a free time at a hair salon and books it.
inputs: the salon, the day, and the time you want
people say:
- I need a trim next week
- Get me in with my usual barber
- I hate waiting, find the first open spot
- Do you have anything on Friday afternoon?
- I want to dye my hair a peach color, book the salon
- Make it a time when the shop is not too busy

Bread and cookies begin as dough, a soft mix of flour, water and other things. Baking changes the dough with heat, and it needs time to rise or rest first. A wet dough feels sticky and makes soft bread, while a dry dough makes hard cookies. Cookies are often shaped into a small round lump the size of a coin. People change the baking time, the heat of the oven, and the size of the batch. They say, 'Set a timer for twenty minutes,' 'Make the oven hotter,' or 'Cancel the timer, the bread is not ready.' They also ask, 'How long should it rise?'

A bike ride is a trip on two wheels, and many people plan it before they go. A route shows the roads and paths to take, how far it is, and how long it should take. Riders often choose public paths that cars cannot use. They change the length, the speed they want to ride at, and the hills they will pass. They say, 'Find me a flat ride of ten miles,' 'Avoid the busy roads,' or 'Block out Sunday morning for a ride.' On rainy days, some people ride an indoor bike, and they put a rug under it to keep the floor safe.

Reading text aloud is a tool for people who cannot see small words well, or who are busy with their hands. The phone reads the screen out loud in a clear voice. People change how fast it reads, how big the text is, and which voice they like. They say, 'Read this page to me,' 'Make the words bigger,' or 'Slow down.' If they are interrupted, they ask, 'Continue where you stopped.' It can read signs and labels too, like a note that says go west, or a recipe that needs one liter of milk. Voice control lets them do all this without touching the screen.
